subject: HelixAI — post-call summary and recommended dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@helixai.com>, Samira Kahn <samira.k@helixai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: HelixAI — post-call summary and recommended dedicated capacity

Hi Evan / Samira —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and the package we think maps to your goals so we can move toward a pilot. TL;DR: recommend a single-tenant dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) sized for steady inference plus a small burst buffer; full isolation and audit logs to meet your regulator requirements.

What we heard (pain points):
- Latency variability during peak batch windows is causing customer-facing timeouts (~200–400ms spikes).
- Need strict tenant isolation due to PHI and contractual segmentation.
- Predictable spend for forecasting billing and procurement.
- Audit trails and encryption-at-rest for security/compliance.

Primary goals you stated:
- Keep 95th percentile token latency below ~100ms for short-form generation flows and below 250ms for long-context scoring.
- Single-tenant pool with VPC peering and no noisy-neighbor risk.
- A pilot window (4–6 weeks) to validate throughput and SLOs before a quarterly reserved commitment.

Redwood recommended config (initial):
- Dedicated pool: 8 x GPU nodes (NVIDIA A100-class equivalence) pinned to HelixAI account, single-tenant.
- Autoscale headroom: +4 ephemeral nodes for burst windows (policy: scale on sustained 75% GPU util for 3 min).
- KV cache + prefix caching enabled for your prompt patterns (expected 25–40% per-token cost reduction).
- Observability: per-route latency dashboards, token-level billing, and evaluation hooks to detect quality regressions.
- Security: VPC-only control plane access, KMS-managed keys, and audit-log push to your SIEM.

SLA targets we can commit for the pilot:
- Availability: 99.95% (monthly)
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency target of < 120ms for baseline short requests; we’ll measure during pilot and set final SLOs for the contract.

Next steps (ask list):
1) Confirm procurement contact and preferred contracting cadence (DocuSign vs MSA + PO).
2) Technical follow-up: Rishi will schedule a 60-min runbook/design session to validate VPC & peering details and model distro.
3) Provide sample peak traces or a short traffic replay (1–2 hours) so we can tune autoscale thresholds.
4) We’ll share a draft SOW and an estimate workbook — see attachments.

Attachments: HelixAI-dedicated-estimate.xlsx (cost/workbook), proposed-mop.pdf (ops playbook)

If that aligns, propose we target a pilot start the week of Mar 8 so procurement and network setup can complete.

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan@helixai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Kahn <samira.k@helixai.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelixAI — post-call summary and recommended dedicated capacity

Thanks Tessa — solid recap, appreciate the clear options. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock the pilot: 

1) Peak profile — our spikes are short (5–10 minutes) but intense during model retrain/ingestion windows. Typical sustained QPS during peak is ~120 requests/sec, median payload is 512 tokens, 10% of calls are long-context (8k tokens) for batch scoring. Will the +4 burst nodes be enough or should we allow for faster scale to +8 if needed?

2) Model runtime — we currently run a mix of fp16 and quantized variants. Please call out any perf differences we should expect when we move to a quantized production variant.

3) Compliance — encryption at rest is required (we have a SOC-affiliated auditor who will request evidence), and we'll need access to audit logs with timestamps. Is log export to our Splunk instance supported?

Procurement: looping Samira to scope contracting. Our preferred cadence is MSA + PO; we typically need 2 weeks for internal sign-off on SOW language.

If you can reply on those three items and share a proposed pilot SLA and timeline, we can review with our infra team on Monday.

—Evan
Head of Infrastructure, HelixAI
Evan.Brooks@helixai.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@helixai.com>, Samira Kahn <samira.k@helixai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelixAI — post-call summary and recommended dedicated capacity

Evan — thanks for the questions, good context. Answers below and actions assigned.

1) Burst sizing: the +4 nodes is our conservative headroom for brief spikes. Given your 120 QPS peak and long-context fraction, I recommend we enable an accelerated burst policy for the pilot: allow scaling to +8 ephemeral nodes with a faster cooldown (scale up at 60% util sustained for 60s). We'll provision autoscaler settings for the pilot so we can observe behavior and adjust before committing. (Action: Rishi to implement pilot autoscale policy).

2) Quantization/perf: quantized variants will reduce GPU memory usage and can increase throughput, but latency per-token can vary by ~5–20% depending on kernel support. For the pilot we'll run your fp16 baseline and a quantized candidate side-by-side. We'll include per-model perf profiles in the SOW so you have clear expectations. (Action: Rishi to capture perf delta matrix).

3) Compliance/logs: yes — encryption at rest via KMS is standard on the private pool offering. We can stream audit logs to your Splunk tenant (we’ll provide log-format spec). Expect a log delivery delay of < 60s for most event types. (Action: Priya to coordinate audit-log setup and provide the KMS/arch spec).

Proposed pilot SLA (formalized in SOW):
- Availability: 99.95% (monthly)
- Observed 95th percentile token latency target: baseline short requests < 120ms; long-context scoring targets to be measured and agreed during pilot.
- Incident response: initial 30-min acknowledgement for Sev1, engineering on-call within 4 hours.

Timeline we recommend:
- Week of Feb 23: Technical runbook session (Rishi) + network checklist completion
- Week of Mar 8: Pilot start (4 weeks)
- End of pilot: measurement review and finalize reserved commitment by Mar 31

Attachments: SOW-draft-HelixAI.docx (draft SOW), HelixAI-dedicated-estimate.xlsx, proposed-mop.pdf

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/helixai/dedicated-estimate (estimate workbook), https://app.redwood.com/sow/HLX-2026-092 (SOW editor)

If this looks right I’ll ask Priya to open the MSA/PO thread and Rishi to send an invite for the runbook session. Proposed meeting windows: Tue Feb 23, 10–11am PT or Wed Feb 24, 2–3pm PT — what works for your infra team?

Best —

Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
